quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle at night instead of during the day, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly.
Leave more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam when possible.
Tailgate other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tailgate other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to avoid crashes. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: What gear should you be in when your motorcycle is stopped?

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Fifth gear.
Any gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: First gear.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: In a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: They should lean together.
They should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider should lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle should lean while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Make sudden movements.
Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.question: How should you brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use only one brake in non-emergency situations.
Use both brakes only when riding on wet pavement.
Always use both brakes.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If one of your tires goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Hold the handgrips loosely.
Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, ease off the throttle and ride straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gradually apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator stop other drivers from sharing their lane?

options.text: Give dirty looks to other drivers.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the left part of the lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to leave little space on either side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: What is the best way to control your motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to prop yourself up instead of steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit far back so you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced in turns. Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect you?

options.text: They make you drowsy.
They make you more alert.
They make you hungry.
They make you unable to focus.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or nerves can cause drowsiness and may impair safe riding. Know how any medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: How much alcohol you drink.
How fast you drink.
Body weight.
Height.

questions.correctAnswerText: Height.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Your eyes and your face.
Your face but not your eyes.
Your eyes, but not your face.
Neither your face nor your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield is needed to protect your entire face in a crash.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you ride?

options.text: In any part of the lane.
In the part of the lane closest to the shoulder.
In the part of the lane where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually, this is the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handle grips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold both handle grips firmly. Ease off the throttle and ride straight. If you must brake, slowly use the brake of the good tire. As you slow down, move to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn
questions.explanation: When your left arm is extended straight out to the left, it tells other riders you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle in the city, how far ahead should you look?

options.text: At least one half block ahead.
About 10 feet ahead.
Behind you.
Less far than on a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least one half block ahead.
questions.explanation: Look at least one half block to one full block ahead. Watch for cars, pedestrians, bicycles, and other hazards. Looking ahead helps you react to problems before you reach them.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What should you NOT tell a passenger to do before riding?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to mount after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold onto the handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: What is the best formation when riding in curves or entering a highway?

options.text: Pairs.
Single-file.
Staggered.
Passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when riding through curves, making turns, or entering or exiting a highway. This is safer than other formations in these situations.

questions.question: When railroad tracks cross your lane at an angle, what is safest?

options.text: Ride straight across within your lane.
It is dangerous to ride straight across.
It is not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Ride on the shoulder of the road to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight across within your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride straight across the tracks while staying in your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle could be dangerous because you might end up in another lane of traffic.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Come to a complete stop.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely and let them go in front of you. Speeding up makes it more dangerous because they will tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What should you do when riding?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from the elements
Taking artificial stimulants
Limiting the distance ridden in one day
Taking frequent breaks

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants
questions.explanation: For long trips, take frequent breaks to rest. Do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Do not take artificial stimulants because they are dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Any time you are slowing or stopping
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you are slowing or stopping
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should riders do at a blind intersection with a stop sign?

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop sign, first stop where the sign indicates. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.
